title: Making Tacking Stitches
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use large needles, thick contrasting thread and a piece of cotton cloth. Count needles in and out at the start and end of every lesson.

skills.key_step: The child identifies even tacking (stitches and spaces the same length), uneven tacking (long stitch, short space) and diagonal tacking (slanting stitches holding layers flat), and says tacking is temporary.

floor.prerequisite: Can measure a length in centimetres.
floor.question: Measure this line in cm.
floor.answer: the length read from the ruler

steps: Look at the stitches and the spaces.
Same length: even. Long and short: uneven. Slanting: diagonal.
contexts: tacking a hem on a school uniform
joining two pieces of a pillow case
holding a lining in a bag

board.do: Draw a line of long stitches with short gaps.
Point at a stitch and a gap.

listen_for: To join the cloth for good
misconceptions.repair: Tack two pieces and sew them, then pull out the tacking.

misconceptions.ask: Which tacking has long stitches on top and short stitches underneath?
misconceptions.repair: Make each tacking on a scrap and compare the top and the back.
Pull out a tacking stitch and then a back stitch and compare.

misconceptions.ask: What is diagonal tacking used for?
misconceptions.repair: Show slanting stitches holding a lining flat; ask why they slope.

checks.question: What are even tacking stitches like?
checks.answer: stitches and spaces the same length

checks.question: Does tacking stay in the finished item?

skills.key_step: The child says how tacking is done (thread the needle, small knot or backstitch, stitches in and out along the line, finish loosely) and that it holds the cloth in place before the final stitching, then is pulled out.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the types of tacking stitches.
floor.question: Which tacking has stitches and spaces the same?

representations: cloth, a large needle and bright thread
a finished sample with the tacking half removed
steps: Thread the needle; start with a small knot.
Sew in and out along the line.
Sew the final seam, then pull the tacking out.

board.do: Draw two cloth pieces tacked together.
Ask what happens to the tacking after the seam is sewn.
Rub the tacking out of the drawing.

listen_for: It is left in the cloth
misconceptions.ask: What is done with the tacking when the sewing is finished?
misconceptions.repair: Show a garment with tacking left in and ask what it looks like.

misconceptions.ask: What comes first, tacking or the final stitching?
misconceptions.repair: Sew two slippery pieces without tacking and see them slide.
Compare how long it takes to unpick tiny stitches and long stitches.

listen_for: With a big knot at each end
misconceptions.ask: How does tacking start and end?
misconceptions.repair: Pull out a tacking thread with and without knots at both ends.

checks.question: Why is tacking done before the final stitching?
checks.answer: to hold the cloth in place

checks.question: Why is tacking done in a bright colour?
checks.answer: so it is easy to see and pull out
